name: kitchensink4word
description: Everything plus the kitchen sink for Microsoft Word. 219 document operations across 108 tools, plus live in-Word editing.
long_description: A Model Context Protocol server for Microsoft Word documents. 219 distinct operations across 108 tools, covering document creation, text and formatting, tables, styles, images, charts, document assembly, headers and footers, footnotes, comments, tracked changes, mail merge, batch operations, redaction, accessibility audit and repair, compliance audits, path sandboxing, and document diagnostics. Tools load in tiers: a 28 tool lite surface opens the session at about 7,700 tokens, and packs are enabled on demand. Live mode edits documents open in Word in place, with each tool call landing as a single undo step; live mode requires Windows with Microsoft Word installed. The file-based majority of the toolset works on any .docx file without Word running. Launching this bundle requires uv (the uvx command) on your machine; the server itself is fetched from PyPI on first launch. Tip: in Claude Desktop's Tool permissions, set the Read-only tools group to Always Allow: those tools cannot change anything, and it stops most permission prompts.

all_tools.title: Load every tool at startup
all_tools.description: On: all 108 tools are loaded when a chat starts, which uses about 26,700 tokens of the conversation before you type anything. Off (recommended): the chat starts with the 28 everyday tools and Claude switches the rest on by itself when a task needs them.

lock_tools.title: Lock the tool set at startup
lock_tools.description: On: whatever tools are loaded when the chat opens are the only tools it can use, and Claude cannot add more. Off (recommended): Claude can switch extra tools on mid-chat when a task calls for them, such as tracked changes or citations.
